subject: english
title: Grammar and Punctuation
description: Lower Key Stage 2 grammar and punctuation: word classes, conjunctions, the a/an rule, inverted commas for speech, and paragraphs (English Appendix 2, Years 3 and 4).

objectives.statement: Identify word classes: nouns, verbs, adjectives and adverbs.
Express time, place and cause using conjunctions, adverbs and prepositions.
Use the forms 'a' or 'an' according to whether the next word begins with a consonant or a vowel sound.
Use and punctuate direct speech with inverted commas (speech marks).
Use paragraphs to organise ideas around a theme.

items.prompt: What word class is 'dog' — a naming word for a person, place or thing?
What word class is 'run' — a doing or being word?
In 'the fluffy cat', which word is the adjective?
In 'She sang loudly', which word is the adverb?

items.statement: An adjective is a word that describes a noun.

items.prompt: Which joining word fits: 'We stayed inside ___ it was raining.'
Which word is a conjunction (a joining word)?
Which conjunction best shows time: 'I brushed my teeth ___ I went to bed.'

items.statement: A conjunction is used to join two parts of a sentence.

items.prompt: Name the word class of 'under' in 'the cat sat under the table' (it shows position).
Choose the correct word: 'I ate ___ apple.'
Choose the correct word: 'She has ___ dog.'

items.statement: We use 'an' before a word that begins with a vowel sound.

items.prompt: Choose the correct word: 'It was ___ hour long.'
Which sentence uses inverted commas (speech marks) correctly?
What punctuation marks go around the exact words a character says out loud?

items.statement: Inverted commas go around the exact words that a person speaks.

items.prompt: What do we call a group of sentences about one idea or theme in a piece of writing?

items.statement: We usually start a new paragraph when we change idea, time or place.

items.prompt: Where should the comma go in this line of speech: '"Wait for me [ ]" she called.'
options: inside the speech marks, before them closing
